title: Microcost heuristics and proposed q-config for batch/cache
content:
Purpose:
This note collects lightweight heuristics and concrete parameter proposals to surface in the new microcost spreadsheet (v3). Goal is to produce a short list of recommended defaults + conditional knobs for three common workload archetypes so the spreadsheet can emit easy-to-read suggested settings (batching, cache rules, q-config) and expected unit-cost deltas. This is a companion/draft input to the experiments Ethan is running (see linked PR) and Priya's eval sets.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus on inference cost per 1M user-requests and per-1M generated-tokens across our hosted and dedicated tiers.
- Target three workload archetypes: realtime chat, async document embeddings, and high-throughput classification/reranking.
- Recommendations aim to be conservative (prioritize reliability) but actionable for product defaults in Optimize UI.

High-level recommendations (one-liners):
- Realtime chat: small per-request batch sizes (1-6), aggressive prefix KV caching for repeated prompts (TTL 30m–24h depending on user), prefer int8 quantization profiles when model validated, avoid int4 as default for completions (use for embeddings if evals confirm).
- Embeddings (async): larger batch windows (64–512 depending on latency tolerance), shared pooling across concurrent requests, use static 4-bit quantization (int4) on embed-only models if end-to-end MSE delta < 0.5% in downstream retrieval.
- Reranking/classification: medium batches (8–64), dynamic batching with a 30–200ms pooling window, KV caching only for repeated contexts, prefer int8 with optional fallback to fp16 on negative regression.

Detailed heuristics and rationale:
1) Batching heuristics
- Latency SLO < 200ms (interactive chat): target batch_size 1–4 on GPU A100/RTX-class with continuous batching disabled except micro-batching. rationale: single-user interactivity penalizes batch wait.
- Latency SLO 200–800ms (mixed chat/assistant): allow batch_size 6–16, pooling window 20–100ms to absorb short bursts.
- Throughput-only (embeddings pipelines): batch_size 64–512, use 2-stage sharding if memory bound.
- Heuristic formula (spreadsheet): suggested_batch = clamp(round( target_tput_per_gpu / expected_concurrent_flows ), 1, 512) where target_tput_per_gpu is precomputed per model/hardware row.

2) Caching heuristics (KV & result cache)
- KV caching: enable by default for chat/history reuse. TTL/buckets: short-session (single conversation) TTL 30m, long-session (persisted conv) TTL 24h. Eviction: LRU by token-length-weighted metric.
- Prefix cache eligibility: mark prompts with stable system + static user instructions as cacheable; ephemeral user context not cacheable.
- Result-level caching (embeddings): fingerprint by input-normalized text + model+qconfig. Cache key expiry: 7d default for embeddings; 0 (disabled) for chat completions except when fingerprinted identical queries.
- Expected cache hit impact (spreadsheet sample): 30% hit rate reduces per-token compute by ~22% for chat workloads (observed in infra tests).

3) Quantization (q-config) guidance
- Profiles: fp16 (baseline), int8 (recommended default where supported), int4 (experimental, embeddings-first).
- Int8: typical perf gains 1.6–2.2x speedup on generative models with <1% measurable quality regression on LM logprob metrics. Use rounded symmetric quantization with per-channel scaling for attention/cross-attention weights.
- Int4: yields 2.8–4x memory reduction, but risk of divergence on long-context generation. Use for embed-only models where retrieval downstream tolerates small noise.
- Fallback policy: automatic fallback to fp16 when model eval regressions exceed thresholds (per-eval suite A/B).

Per-archetype suggested presets (to be encoded as rows in spreadsheet):
- Realtime Chat (preset: chat-small-latency)
  - batch_policy: micro (max_batch=6, pooling_ms=30)
  - kv_cache: enabled (session_ttl=30m, persist=false)
  - q_profile: int8-default (fallback=fp16)
  - expected_delta: -18% cost, +0.4% quality risk (probabilistic)

- Embeddings Async (preset: embeddings-throughput)
  - batch_policy: throughput (max_batch=256, pooling_ms=200)
  - kv_cache: disabled for embeddings results unless idempotent input
  - q_profile: int4-embed (validation_required=true)
  - expected_delta: -42% cost, quality risk <0.3% MSE if validated

- Reranking / Batch Classification (preset: rerank-medium)
  - batch_policy: balanced (max_batch=64, pooling_ms=50)
  - kv_cache: conditional (cache identical contexts for 1h)
  - q_profile: int8-safe (fallback=fp16 on regession)
  - expected_delta: -26% cost, quality risk ~0.8% on re-rank NDCG

Cost model spreadsheet guidance (what to include in v3):
- Required columns per model/hardware row: model_name, model_size, tokens_per_second_fp16, tokens_per_second_int8, tokens_per_second_int4, memory_fp16, memory_int8, memory_int4, baseline_cost_per_hour_fp16, batch_optimal_range, suggested_batch, pooling_ms.
- Workload simulator section: users_per_minute, avg_tokens_per_request, pct_with_context_reuse, pct_concurrent, sla_latency_ms. Spreadsheet should compute estimated GPU-hours, cost_by_config, delta_vs_baseline, and ROI-breakpoints where switching q-profile saves >X% cost.
- Include sample tabs: one for chat sample day (1M requests), one for embeddings pipeline (100M vectors), and one for reranking experiment (500k requests).

Open questions / risk items:
- How to automatically detect "cacheable" prompt fingerprints in presence of minor personalization? (Priya to prototype a lightweight heuristics classifier.)
- Int4 failure modes: need to standardize regression suite (long-tail prompts + token-level surprisal checks). Define pass/fail thresholds.
- Billing attribution: do we expose cost-savings by q-profile to end-customers or keep internal? Legal/pricing implications.

Quick experiments to run (owners & rough timeline):
- E1: embedding int4 pilot on 2 models across 3 datasets (owner: Priya, 2 weeks). Output: acceptance thresholds spreadsheet + sample lost-recall metric.
- E2: chat micro-batching latency sweep across 0–100ms pooling windows on A100 (owner: Ethan, 1 week). Output: latency distribution CSV + recommended pooling_ms per model.
- E3: KV cache hit-rate synthetic test (owner: Liam, 10 days). Mix of session lengths and personalization to estimate realistic hit curve.

Action items / next steps:
- Add these presets as new tab in cost-model-microcost-v3.xlsx (Ethan).
- Wire preset -> Optimize UI suggestion mapping (Product Eng + UX) for beta.
- Run Priya's embed int4 pilot and record acceptance thresholds; block/apply to spreadsheet.
- Create a short internal one-pager for sales/CS describing real-world tradeoffs and recommended defaults for onboarding.

Appendix: sample calculation (chat example)
- Assumptions: 1M chat requests/day, avg 80 tokens generated, baseline fp16 throughput 400 tokens/s on model X, int8 throughput 700 tokens/s, GPU cost $3.00/hr.
- Baseline GPU-hours: total_tokens = 1M * 80 = 80M tokens. time_fp16 = 80M / 400 = 200k seconds = 55.6 GPU-hr. cost_fp16 = 55.6 * $3 = $166.7/day.
- Int8 time = 80M / 700 = 114.3k s = 31.7 GPU-hr. cost_int8 = 31.7 * $3 = $95.1/day. delta = -$71.6/day (-43%).
- If micro-batching adds 10% additional wait but increases batching efficiency to effectively reduce compute by extra 5%, include that under "expected_delta" in presets.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and not a formal playbook. Please comment with concrete empirical thresholds you’ve observed (e.g., pooling_ms where p99 breaks for you) rather than abstract preferences.
- If we lock presets in the Optimize UI, ensure we provide an "advanced" toggle so customers can override pooling and q-profile per-deployment.

End of draft.
